html:
In 146 BCE Roman armies destroyed two great cities, Carthage in North Africa and Corinth in Greece. The year marks the Roman Republic's rise to mastery of the Mediterranean.

  • Carthage had lost the First and Second Punic Wars but recovered as a trading city. Cato the Elder is remembered for ending his speeches with "Carthage must be destroyed". Rome found a pretext and began the Third Punic War in 149 BCE. After a three-year siege, Scipio Aemilianus stormed the city. Survivors were sold as slaves and the city razed. Its land became the Roman province of Africa.
  • The same year, the general Lucius Mummius crushed the Achaean League and sacked Corinth. Its men were killed, its women and children enslaved, and its art shipped to Rome. Greece came under Roman control.

Julius Caesar refounded both cities as Roman colonies in 44 BCE. The wealth and slaves that poured into Rome fed the strains behind the Gracchan land law a few years later.
sum: In 146 BCE Roman armies destroyed two great cities, Carthage in North Africa and Corinth in Greece. The year marks the Roman Republic's rise to mastery of the Mediterranean.
